title: Recovery readiness
tenantScope: Can every backup of {tenant} be restored today?
subtitle: Random mails, files, calendar items and contacts are read back from each latest backup through the restore path and compared byte by byte with their checksums. Only a proven restore counts: a backup no check has read back yet, even one taken after a successful check, is shown as not proven.

actions.verifyNowFor: Check now: the latest backup of {name}
actions.viewPreviousReportFor: Report of the previous backup's check for {name}

green.title: The latest restore point of every object passed its restore check
green.description: {total, plural, one {The protected object} other {All # protected objects}} passed the latest restore check.

yellow.title: Restorable, but something needs attention
yellow.description: {count, plural, one {# object needs} other {# objects need}} attention: a warning in the latest check, or a check that is overdue.

red.title: Not every backup is proven restorable
red.description: {count, plural, one {# object cannot be restored completely, or its latest backup is} other {# objects cannot be restored completely, or their latest backups are}} not proven restorable yet. A backup without a passed restore check counts as failed.

empty.title: Nothing protected yet
empty.description: Once mailboxes, drives, IMAP accounts or machines are protected and backed up, their restore checks appear here.

unverified.title: {count, plural, one {The latest backup of # object is not verified yet} other {The latest backups of # objects are not verified yet}}
unverified.description: {count, plural, one {This backup was taken after the last restore check. Until a check reads it back, it counts as not proven, whatever an earlier backup scored.} other {These backups were taken after the last restore check. Until a check reads them back, they count as not proven, whatever an earlier backup scored.}}

storage.title: Storage integrity
storage.description: Every pack file is read from each repository and checked against its recorded SHA-256: a sample every week, all packs every month. Damage is repaired from an intact copy where one exists.
storage.never: No storage check has run yet.
storage.corruptTitle: {count, plural, one {# pack is damaged} other {# packs are damaged}}
storage.corrupt: No intact copy exists in any repository, so the damage could not be repaired. Every object whose data sits in these packs is rated not restorable.
storage.corruptHeal: A full backup of the affected objects writes the damaged content again from the source, as far as the source still holds it. Backups no longer reuse data from these packs. Once no backup needs a damaged pack any more, the next storage check retires it.
storage.retired: {count, plural, one {# damaged pack is} other {# damaged packs are}} no longer needed: later backups wrote their content again. {count, plural, one {It was} other {They were}} removed from the index and {count, plural, one {its file is} other {their files are}} deleted by a storage check one day later at the earliest.
storage.repairedTitle: {count, plural, one {# pack was repaired} other {# packs were repaired}}
storage.repaired: A repository held a damaged or missing copy; it was rewritten from an intact copy and read back to confirm.

targetStatus.index_mismatch: contents differ from the chunk index

storage.morePacks: {count, plural, one {and # more pack} other {and # more packs}}
